name: IconButton

knownIssues.summary: Takes the legacy `appearance` (default | primary | subtle) while Figma has moved it to `tone` and `prominence` (tone-is-meaning).

useCases: A familiar action whose icon is clear on its own: search, edit, close, more actions
A compact row of actions, such as a toolbar or a table row
Opening a menu from a "more actions" icon, with isExpanded

figmaSource.notes: The Figma `tone` variant `inverse` maps to the code-level `isInverse` boolean (an orthogonal on-dark treatment), not to a code `appearance` value. The inverse variants mirror the `subtle` tone (transparent fill) retinted to the inverse content + white subtle overlay tokens.

isInverse.description: Orthogonal on-dark treatment for placement on dark/bold surfaces such as Banner - transparent fill, inverse content, and the color-background-neutral-overlay-subtle-* overlays on hover/press/expanded. Flattened by disabled like the appearance.

behaviorRules: Uses aria-label as default tooltip content when tooltip is omitted.
Does not infer tooltip text from aria-labelledby.
Forwarded ref resolves to the native button.
Supports isInverse (boolean) as an orthogonal on-dark treatment for placement on dark/bold surfaces such as Banner; flattened by disabled like the appearance.
do: Name the action in aria-label, which is both the accessible name and the tooltip.
Name the action ("Delete matter"), not the icon ("Trash").
Use Button with a visible label when the icon alone doesn't say what happens.
Use Toggle Icon Button for something that stays on, so it's announced as pressed.
Set isExpanded on a button that opens a menu or panel, and use MoreVertIcon for "more actions".
Set tooltip (or tooltip={false}) yourself when the button is named with aria-labelledby.
dont: Do not put the name only in tooltip: it describes the button only while it shows, so the button has no name.
Do not rely on the tooltip to explain an unfamiliar icon.
Do not show a state by switching the appearance, which assistive technology can't hear.
Do not use Icon Button for navigation: it's a native button and can't be opened in a new tab (use Link Button).
Do not use it for a destructive action that needs a warning or error look: there's no tone, so use a labelled Button.
Do not mix square and round shapes in one toolbar.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a native button.
Defaults to type button.
Forwards its ref to the native button.
Renders children as the icon content, hidden from assistive technology.
Supports aria-label and aria-labelledby as the accessible name.
Uses a string aria-label as the default tooltip content.
Uses custom tooltip content without changing the accessible name.
tooltip={false} suppresses tooltip rendering.
Does not infer tooltip text from aria-labelledby.
Skips its own tooltip inside an external Tooltip.
Supports appearances default, primary, subtle.
Supports sizes xs, sm, md, lg as a fixed square on the Button control heights.
Supports shapes square and round.
Supports isInverse for placement on dark or bold surfaces.
Uses native disabled and suppresses click while disabled.
Shows a tooltip on hover while disabled.
Renders Spinner and sets aria-busy while loading, suppressing click without disabling the button.
isExpanded sets aria-expanded (true or false); an aria-expanded a wrapper passes is kept when isExpanded is unset.
Applies shared focus ring classes.
Uses semantic tokens for sizing, radius, and color.
